rootCause: src/session.ts renamed the public field `token` to `accessToken` on the class `Session`, and two readers in src/auth.ts still read `.token`. The class also carries five ECMAScript private fields (`#secret`, `#refresh`, `#issuedAt`, `#expiresAt`, `#attempts`) against three public members, so its property list is majority-private. Separately and independently, src/contact.ts dereferences the result of `currentProfile()`, an expression with no printable name, which TypeScript reports as TS2531 rather than TS18047.
expectedFix: Rename the two reads in src/auth.ts to `accessToken`, or rename the field back to `token` in src/session.ts. The TS2531 in src/contact.ts is a second, unrelated bug: guard the `contact` before reading `.email`.
purpose: Two witnesses that only real code produced, committed so neither can regress silently. (1) ECMAScript private fields are filtered out of a property list: without the filter this class renders `8 properties: #secret, #refresh, #issuedAt, #expiresAt, #attempts, accessToken, userId, renew`, spending five of eight slots on names no caller may write, and burying `accessToken` — the fact that explains the failure. Found on hono, where 9 of the 12 displayed names were `#`-private and `#req` sat next to the missing `req`. TypeScript's own `private` modifier is deliberately NOT filtered and this fixture does not test it. (2) TS2531 `Object is possibly 'null'` is the ANONYMOUS half of the 18047 family: `currentProfile().contact` has no printable name, so TypeScript drops the `{0}` template, and with no quoted expression there is no anchor for the 18047 resolver to check itself against. It must stay an isolated root — 2531/2532/2533 can never enter CONTEXT_CAPTURE_CODES, and that is a structural fact, not an omission to be corrected later.
